# c10 — SUYU-GURecomp facts vs. MHGU 1.4.0 disassembly

Source: SUYU-GURecomp commit 35015f1, `game_settings.cpp` (debug-probe / hook-mark sites around the viewport-scissor setter). Address convention: SUYU "main+X" equals our vaddr X. Facts recorded in own words; no SUYU code copied.

| vaddr | meaning | SUYU cite | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0xbc1204 | Viewport/scissor setter probe point placed just after the routine's first indirect call (return site of `blx r7` at 0xbc1200); SUYU uses it as a coverage/probe mark (RecompHooks::Mark sets a bit, any interior pc is valid) and documents it as "after its first call", so no function-entry claim exists | game_settings.cpp:1332-1333, game_settings.h:338, recomp_hooks.cpp:29-38 | VERIFIED | `bc1200: blx r7` immediately precedes `bc1204: ldr r8, [sp, #8]`; interior of a 148-byte-frame routine (epilogue at 0xbc13c0) |
| 0xbc12d0 | SUYU annotates this offset (paired with 0xbc13bc) as holding the draw-state object in r10 for the viewport/scissor setter; our disassembly is a mid-routine rect-clamp sequence operating on r10-backed state, consistent but not naming-provable | game_settings.cpp:1380 (comment) | PLAUSIBLE | `add r0, r10, #56` / `addne r0, r10, #72` then `ldm r0 {r4, r5}` pick one of two field pairs on a flag, and `ldr r0, [r0, #12]` / `cmps r0, lr` / `movlt lr, r0` / `cmps r2, lr` / `movwgt r2, #0x0` / `movwgt lr, #0x0` clamp two values against bounds before `ldr r0, [pc, #216]` pulls the data pointer 0xc7df94 — a min/max clamp over r10-relative fields, exactly what a viewport/scissor setter does, though no `push` here either so the SUYU offset is interior to the routine, not an entry |
| 0xbc13bc | Second address of the same SUYU probe pair: the tail of the setter, where the r10 object pointer is written back into the context struct and the frame is torn down; confirms r10 is a persistent draw-state object, but the viewport semantics still come from SUYU, not from these instructions | game_settings.cpp:1380 (comment) | PLAUSIBLE | `str r10, [r9, #8]` persists the object through the r9 context, immediately followed by `add sp, sp, #148` / `pop {r4, r5, r6, r7, r8, r9, r10, r11, pc}` — the routine epilogue matching the 148-byte frame, so 0xbc12d0 and 0xbc13bc are two offsets inside one routine whose real entry precedes 0xbc1204; the literal-pool words that follow (0x00c7e3ac, 0x00c7e1a8, 0x00c7df94, 0x00c80498) are data pointers, and 0xbc13e0 starts the next function with `push {r4, r5, r6, r7, r8, lr}` / `sub sp, sp, #16` |
